suggestions.what: What each item is for, said in the item
suggestions.why: The resistant starch item read Human Low on its own in the leaky gut list. With its reason as a plain clause, "your body can't digest it, so it all goes to them", the Low was gone, but the two short items still read Medium together. Beta-glucans was the one item in the list that never said why you'd take it. Now it does: in gut tissue taken from people, a yeast beta-glucan kept the lining from leaking when it was stressed (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166688). With both, the whole list reads Human, High.

suggestions.title: Phase 4 opens each organ case on what you'd have

edits.before: So check your organs (Brown). Is it Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency? You'd test for that with Stool Elastase, and treat it with high-dose enzymes. Or is it Bile Acid Diarrhea? That test is SeHCAT, and the treatment is bile binders.
edits.after: So check your organs (Brown). If your pancreas doesn't make enough digestive enzymes, called Exocrine Pancreatic Insufficiency, you'd test for that with Stool Elastase, and treat it with high-dose enzymes. If it's Bile Acid Diarrhea, the test is SeHCAT, and the treatment is bile binders.

suggestions.title: If you're pregnant: skip berberine, and why

edits.before: Some severe symptoms warrant seeing a doctor rather than considering this DIY approach at the moment. Take it seriously if you notice blood in your stool (if it's blood from upper digestive tract, it could be smelly, black & tarry, not red like from lower GI). Other serious signs to note: losing weight fast, severe pain, a fever or dehydration. And if you're pregnant, some herbs and supplements, like berberine, aren't safe. If your immune system is weak, some probiotics could be risky, since they're live bacteria that need to be kept in check to prevent overgrowth. If you have an IBD flare, cancer or another serious illness, the standard disclaimer applies: work out what to take with your doctor instead of putting a stack together yourself.
edits.after: Some severe symptoms warrant seeing a doctor rather than considering this DIY approach at the moment. Take it seriously if you notice blood in your stool (if it's blood from upper digestive tract, it could be smelly, black & tarry, not red like from the lower digestive tract). Other serious signs to note: losing weight fast, severe pain, a fever or dehydration. And if you're pregnant or breastfeeding, skip berberine, which can give a newborn jaundice, and ask your doctor about any other herb or supplement first. suggestions.why: "And if you're pregnant, some herbs and supplements, like berberine, aren't safe." read Medium: a warning that doesn't say what to do. Now it says what to do and why: skip berberine, which can give a newborn jaundice, and ask your doctor about the rest. NCCIH says people who are pregnant or breastfeeding should not use berberine (https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/in-the-news-berberine), so breastfeeding is in it too.
